correctness.rationale: For arbitrary complex a,b,c,d, multiplication by one phase and independent rotations of z,w reduce nonzero reference terms to A+Bz+Cw+D exp(i phi)zw with A,B,C,D≥0; zero-coefficient cases follow by continuity. For each |z|=1, maximize exactly in w: F(z)=|A+Bz|+|C+D exp(i phi)z|. At z±=±exp(−i phi/2), set X± and Y± to the two moduli. Exact antipodal square identities give X+²+X−²=2(A²+B²), Y+²+Y−²=2(C²+D²). Triangle inequality on the SUM of two complex products gives X+Y+ +X−Y−≥2(AC+BD). Consequently F(z+)²+F(z−)²≥(A+B+C+D)²+(A−B+C−D)² and one sample F≥mass/sqrt2. The witness P*=1+z+w−zw gives F(z)=|1+z|+|1−z|≤2sqrt2 with equality at z=i, so coefficient mass 4 and Sidon quotient sqrt2. The calculation proves the full infinite torus and all complex coefficients without relying on finite sampling. Independent algebraic reconstruction checked phase conventions, triangle signs, sum-of-squares normalization and the endpoint zero-coefficient domain; 25,000 deterministic independent random choices checked the two-point inequality and the witness as corroboration, not proof.
residual_risks: A numerical checker alone cannot prove the universal statement; the independent complete analytic argument supplies that proof.
Only the four-corner free two-torus support is proved; no arbitrary 4-frequency theorem, other finite-group constant, or full equality-case classification follows.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge independent statement/implication comparison did not identify a covering prior theorem for the sharp four-corner two-torus coefficient-ell1 inequality with ALL complex coefficients. The primary three-character Sidon theorem, 2x2 real-coefficient bilinear extreme-point/Littlewood-4/3 analysis, homogeneous-polynomial asymptotic bounds, and the one-variable four-character discussion have different quantified sets or coefficient functionals. A directly overlapping published four-corner Fourier p-moment phase theorem optimizes finite-p moments at fixed magnitudes and explicitly excludes p=infinity: it does not establish the sharp unconstrained coefficient-mass/sup-norm ratio. Finite cyclic phase-only Fourier-zero and binary flat-spectrum results similarly do not imply this continuous torus constant. An older equivalent complex 2x2 injective/projective tensor norm formula remains a genuine residual bibliographic risk; unsuccessful searches are not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The finite four-corner Cartesian support is a canonical non-dissociated Fourier configuration in rank two: its cross phase ad/(bc) is the first genuinely coupled coefficient invariant, so the exact ell1-versus-uniform norm is a natural structural question in Fourier Sidon theory and in 2x2 complex bilinear/tensor norms. Unlike a routine parameter substitution, the proof derives a universal sharp constant for arbitrary complex magnitudes and phases with a new two-antipodal-phase certificate and explicit extremal Hadamard sign pattern. The precise value is independently useful as a small-scale benchmark for sparse harmonic inequalities and comparisons against finite cyclic discretizations and one-dimensional four-frequency families. It is a motivated exact self-contained constant, despite not establishing an overarching n×m theorem or novel equality classification. Correctness or reproduction alone was not treated as value.
residual_risks: The mathematical proof is short and draws on classical parallelogram/triangle methods; the claim is valuable as an exact natural invariant rather than a broad advance.
If an older identical complex 2x2 norm formula is located, the originality and independent-value novelty assessment must be reconsidered.
